question: A postural blood pressure drop of 20 mmHg systolic (or 10 mmHg diastolic) on standing indicates significant intravascular volume depletion and is an indication for urgent IV fluid resuscitation in a patient with GI bleeding.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Postural hypotension is defined as a ≥20 mmHg systolic (or ≥10 mmHg diastolic) drop on standing and reliably identifies 15–20% blood volume loss — the threshold at which haemodynamic compensation begins to fail. It is the single most informative clinical sign for volume assessment at the bedside.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Postural hypotension (≥20 mmHg systolic or ≥10 mmHg diastolic fall on standing) reflects a blood volume deficit of approximately 15–20% and indicates significant haemodynamic compromise. This is a reliable early sign of volume depletion before supine hypotension develops, and mandates immediate resuscitation.
